Two invoices are open on that account: IB-1412 against DL-8726 and IB-8366 against DL-1900. Each carries a line 'Clearance handling fee'. That is Marrowby Arc's own service charge for presenting the entry to customs. It is not duty or tax, and customs neither sets nor receives it, so please do not describe it as a customs charge. It appears in the fee schedule of the emailed quote. The fee can be reviewed, invoice by invoice, where the customer prepared the entry documents himself. To open a review we need two things: the number of the invoice he is disputing, or both, and a copy of the customs clearance notice for that consignment showing who is named as declarant. We do not hold the notice when a customer self-files. No review is open and we cannot say what the outcome would be.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask him which invoice he is disputing (IB-1412, IB-8366 or both) and to upload the customs clearance notice again because it did not arrive, so Import billing can open a review.

must: Asks Marisol Grimshaw which invoice he is disputing: IB-1412 (DL-8726), IB-8366 (DL-1900), or both.
Tells him the clearance notice did not arrive with his message and asks him to upload it again, for the consignment or consignments he is disputing.
Describes the line accurately as Marrowby Arc's own clearance handling fee, not a duty or tax, and says that Import billing decide the review and that the outcome is not known.
must_not: Calls the fee a customs charge, duty, tax or government fee, or lets his description of it as a 'customs fee' stand as the desk's own wording.
Promises that the fee will be removed, reduced or refunded, or says a review has been opened.
Forwards the dispute to Import billing as though the clearance notice and invoice number had been supplied.
Tells him the fee was in the quote and so nothing can be done, when Import billing have said it can be reviewed for self-prepared entries.
Asks him for more than the two items Import billing named, such as identity documents or the full set of customs forms.
Treats the repeated copy of the request as a second, separate request (for example by sending two requests to the same team)
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Thank you for coming back on this. I asked Import billing about the charge. The line on your invoices reads 'Clearance handling fee'. It is Marrowby Arc's own service charge for presenting the entry to customs; it is not a duty or tax, and customs does not set or receive it. Import billing tell me this fee can be reviewed where the customer prepared the entry documents himself, which is what you describe. To open that review they need two things from you. First, which invoice you are disputing: IB-1412 for consignment DL-8726, IB-8366 for DL-1900, or both. Second, the customs clearance notice for that consignment, or for each one. Your last message reached me with no attachment, so please upload the notice again here. Once I have both I will pass them to Import billing. The decision is theirs and I cannot tell you in advance what it will be.
